newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. chief's Cyprus adviser briefs council president.
newsitem.headline: U.N. chief's Cyprus adviser briefs council president.

text.p: The U.N. secretary-general's special adviser for Cyprus, former Ecuador Foreign Minister Diego Cordovez, has briefed the president of the Security Council on preparations for forthcoming talks between the leaders of the island's Greek and Turkish communities, U.N. spokesman Fred Eckhard said on Thursday.

The talks, set for July 9-13, will be the first known meeting in nearly three years between Cypriot President Glafcos Clerides, representing the Greek Cypriots, and Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash.
The United Nations is trying to revive long-stalled negotiations on reuniting the divided island under a bi-communal, bi-zonal federation.

Eckhard confirmed next month's talks would take place in "upstate New York," but still declined to disclose the precise location. The United Nations is trying to keep the negotiations as secluded as possible.
There has been strong speculation they would take place at a conference centre at Harriman, New York, on the estate of the late U.S. statesman and diplomat Averell Harriman.

The Security Council, whose president this month is ambassador Sergei Lavrov of Russia, had been expected to hold private consultations on Cyprus on Thursday. But this was postponed until next Monday, Eckhard said.

The council would by then have a report by Secretary-General Kofi Annan on his good offices role in promoting a settlement of the Cyprus problem. It would also discuss a report issued last week recommending another six-month renewal, until December 31, of the 1,200-member U.N. Peacekeeping Force stationed in Cyprus since 1964.
